steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Voltages above 50 V AC or 120 V DC are considered hazardous; always work on low-voltage circuits when possible.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Isolation means disconnecting equipment from all energy sources before working on it; use lock-out/tag-out procedures.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An earth bond provides a low-resistance path for fault currents, causing protective devices (fuses, MCBs) to operate quickly.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Double-insulated equipment (Class II) has reinforced insulation and no earth connection; identified by the square-within-square symbol.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why must a 1 MΩ resistor be present in an antistatic wrist strap lead? | Q: What is the purpose of fume extraction when soldering? | Q: State three hazards associated with soldering and a control measure for each.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: The 1 MΩ resistor limits current to a safe level if the wearer accidentally touches a live conductor, preventing electric shock while still discharging static. | Fume extraction removes rosin-based flux fumes from the breathing zone, preventing respiratory irritation and potential long-term health effects. | Burns from the iron (use stand, keep iron away from skin), fume inhalation (use fume extraction), and lead exposure (wash hands, use lead-free solder).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When discussing ESD, always mention the antistatic wrist strap, mat and storage bags together. For soldering safety, cover all three hazards: burns, fumes and lead exposure. Risk assessment questions require a structured answer: identify hazards, evaluate risk, implement controls. Know the difference between Class I (earthed) and Class II (double-insulated) equipment. Mention CO2 fire extinguishers specifically for electrical fires — never water on electrical fires.
